whats_changed: A deploy landed this week (first one since 07-08/07-10) — 14 code changes covering accessibility labeling, a new security header (Content-Security-Policy), a performance diet on the Explore page, comparison-page editorial sections, and a couple of SEO/growth fixes. Today's full test pass found 0 regressions from any of it.

The Hindi-body-copy gap (English headline/description showing on Hindi pages) is now confirmed on a 5th distinct destination, unchanged in scope — this is a translation-wiring bug, not a data problem (the Hindi text is sitting in the database, correctly written, just not being used by that part of the page).

Two of today's 10 sampled destinations loaded slowly on the very first request (about 3-5 seconds) because they're low-traffic pages that get built on-demand the first time anyone visits them that day — the second request for each was back to normal (under a quarter of a second). Not a problem, just how the caching works for rarely-visited pages.
risks: The accessibility/performance audit is 77 days stale, and this week's deploy is the first in over a week to touch exactly the kind of code (labeling, page-weight) that audit would check. Every day this is deferred, more shipped work goes unverified by it. Recommend scheduling the dedicated deep-audit session referenced in past reports rather than deferring it again.

The Hindi headline/description gap affects the large majority of destination pages (525 of 533 have the Hindi text ready in the database but unused) — this is a visible quality issue for any Hindi-reading visitor landing on a destination page, even though the page technically 'works' (loads, is in Hindi in the browser tab and navigation).
bottom_line: No action required on today's findings — everything that could regress from this week's deploy was checked and came back clean.
